name: おこのみ魂　悟空 (Okonomi-damashii Goku)

claims.text: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki here is finished with a standard okonomiyaki/soy-based sauce, which contains wheat; the batter and noodles are also wheat.

name: お好み・鉄板焼道場 三箆 (Okonomi Teppanyaki Dojo Mihera)

claims.text: Wheat-flour okonomiyaki batter and wheat noodles are cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside all other dishes, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-based; no wheat-free sauce alternative is documented.
The single shared teppan is used for pork, chicken, seafood and egg, so any non-meat item would be cooked on the same surface as animal products.

name: お好み焼き じゅにあ (Okonomiyaki Junia)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki and Fuchu-yaki are finished with a standard sweet okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-and-soy based; the dishes are also built on wheat batter and wheat noodles.
The signature Fuchu-yaki is made with beef-fat mince, and a shared teppan is used for all dishes including meat, egg, and noodles, so vegan separation is not feasible.

name: お好み焼 きしべ (Okonomiyaki Kishibe)

claims.text: Everything is cooked on a single shared teppan griddle where wheat-batter okonomiyaki and wheat noodles are prepared, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with sweet Otafuku-style okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-based.
The shared griddle and dishes routinely involve pork, egg and seafood, so vegan cross-contact cannot be avoided.

name: お好み焼まとちゃん (Okonomiyaki Matochan)

claims.text: Core dishes (okonomiyaki batter, layered wheat noodles, deep-fried あげおこ, and breaded fried oysters) are all wheat-based and cooked on shared teppan/fryer surfaces; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
Dishes are finished with wheat-based okonomiyaki/Otafuku sauce and soy-sauce-based seasonings (e.g., ponzu), which typically contain wheat.
The menu is built around egg, pork, oysters, squid, shrimp, and fish-based dashi/toppings cooked on a shared griddle; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板串焼き やまだ (Okonomiyaki Teppan Kushiyaki Yamada)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki batter and the topping noodles are wheat-based and cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside many other dishes, so cross-contact with gluten is effectively unavoidable.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki sauce, which is typically wheat/soy-based; no gluten-free sauce is documented.
Pork, beef, chicken, egg, and local oysters are cooked on the same shared teppan as any vegetable dishes, so cross-contact with animal products is likely.
The menu page notes that some vegetarian options are available, so a flexitarian diner may find a few plant-leaning dishes by asking.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板焼 福ちゃん (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Fukuchan)

claims.text: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is assembled on a shared griddle from a wheat-flour batter and includes wheat noodles, so heavy gluten cross-contact on the cook surface is inherent.
The okonomiyaki/teppanyaki style relies on a wheat-based savory sauce (the house sauce is described as oyster-and-lemon based); assume the sauce contains wheat.
The griddle is oiled with pork lard and the house sauce uses Hiroshima oysters, so vegan diners face animal-product contact across the cooking surface and seasonings.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板焼 福ちゃん エキエ (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Fukuchan Ekie)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki batter, noodles, and the finishing sauce all contain wheat, and the griddle is shared across wheat-based dishes, so heavy cross-contamination should be assumed for anyone avoiding gluten.
Okonomiyaki sauce and the butter-soy-sauce oyster dish use standard Japanese soy/okonomi sauces, which contain wheat.
The shared griddle cooks pork, oysters, wagyu and other seafood alongside any vegetable items, and okonomiyaki uses egg and fish-based dashi, so animal-product cross-contact is unavoidable.
English and simplified-Chinese menus are available, which makes it easier to ask questions about ingredients.
